Finite-Tailed CDF-Quantile Distributions

The CDF of the CDF-Quantile family (Smithson and Shou, 2017) is G(x,μ,σ)=F[U(H−1(x),μ,σ)],G(x,\mu,\sigma) = F[U(H^{ - 1}(x),\mu,\sigma)],for x∈[0,1]x \in \left[ {0,1} \right], real location parameter μ\mu, and dispersion parameter σ>0\sigma > 0. FF and HH are standard symmetrical CDFs with support on the real line. the default UU function isU(y,μ,σ)=(y−μ)/σU(y,\mu ,\sigma) = (y - \mu)/\sigmaThe finite-tailed subfamily comprises distributions that have defined finite densities at 0 and at 1. These include any combination of the standard Cauchy and Arcsinh distributions for FF and HH, and the t distribution with with 2 degrees of freedom for both FF and HH (i.e., Arcsinh-Arcsinh, Arcsinh-Cauchy, Cauchy-Arcsinh, Cauchy-Cauchy, and t2-t2).

The finite-tailed subfamily, FTCDFQ (Smithson and Shou, 2024), employs functions of a skew parameter, θ\theta. There are four alternative locations for these functions, two with mappings V:[0,1]→[0,1]V:\left[ {0,1} \right] \to \left[ {0,1} \right] applied to xx or to FF, and two with mappings W:ℝ→ℝW:\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} applied to H−1H^{-1} or to UU. Each pair’s function thus has an “inner” and an “outer” position. The inner-position VV is applied to xx and the outer-position VV is applied to FF. Likewise, the inner-position WW is applied to H−1H^{-1} and the outer-position WW is applied to UU. Given that the skew parameter θ\theta also influences location, 2-parameter as well as 3-parameter distributions are viable, i.e., G(x,θ,σ)G\left( {x,\theta ,\sigma } \right) and G(x,μ,θ,σ)G\left( {x,\mu,\theta ,\sigma } \right).

VV is the so-called ``tilt’’ parameter function: V(y,θ)=eθy/(eθy+1−y),V(y,\theta) = e^{\theta}y/(e^{\theta}y + 1 - y),for real θ\theta. It satisfies the requirements of being monotone nondecreasing in yy and V(0,θ)=0V(0,\theta) = 0 and V(1,θ)=1V(1,\theta) = 1. Its derivative has limits eθe^\theta as yy goes to 0 and e−θe^{-\theta} as yy goes to 1. WW is is a modified version of a 2-parameter transformation, sinh⁡(θ+δsinh⁡−1(y))\sinh( \theta + \delta\sinh^{ - 1}(y)), for real θ\theta and δ>0\delta>0, where θ\theta acts as a skew parameter and δ\delta controls tail thickness. Fixing δ=1\delta=1 gives W(y,θ)=sinh⁡(θ+sinh⁡−1(y)),W(y,\theta) = \sinh(\theta + \sinh^{ - 1}(y)),whose derivative has limits eθe^\theta as yy goes to ∞\infty and e−θe^{-\theta} as yy goes to −∞-\infty.

Smithson and Shou (2024) show that the inner-position WW and VV functions are equivalent when the HH function is ArcSinh, and likewise the outer-position WW and VV functions are equivalent when the FF function is ArcSinh. Thus, the FTCDFQ family has two sets of 16 distinct distributions.

Extended-Support Distributions

Kosmidis and Zeileis (2025) developed a method of extending the support beyond 0 and 1 for distributions with support on the unit interval. Their approach is applicable to any distribution whose support is (0,1)(0,1) or [0,1][0,1]. They applied their method to the beta distribution and implemented it in the betareg package. In this package the method is applied to the 2-parameter FTCDFQ distributions. Let ff denote a pdf of xx whose support is the compact unit interval, with a vector of parameters $\bf{\beta}$. Let FF denote the cdf, and F−1F^{-1} the quantile function. An extended support pdf whose distribution follows ff will have support on [−u,u+1][-u, u+1] for u>0u > 0. Denoting the extended support pdf by tt, we define it as a censored version of ff on [−u,u+1][-u, u+1]: t(x,u,β)=F(u/(2u+1),β),x=0t(x,u,β)=f((u+x)/(2u+1),β),x∈(0,1)t(x,u,β)=1−F((u+1)/(2u+1),β),x=1\begin{array}{cl} t(x,u,\beta) = F(u/(2u+1),\beta), x = 0\\ t(x,u,\beta) = f((u+x)/(2u+1),\beta),x \in \left( {0,1} \right)\\ t(x,u,\beta) = 1 - F((u+1)/(2u+1),\beta),x = 1 \end{array} We also have the following identity for the extended-support distribution tt: $${T^{ - 1}}\left( {\gamma ,u,{\bf{\beta }}} \right) = \left( {2u + 1} \right){F^{ - 1}}\left( {\gamma ,{\bf{\beta }}} \right) - u$$ for γ∈(0,1)\gamma \in \left( {0,1} \right), where T−1T^{-1} denotes the quantile function for tt. This equation identifies the linear shift between the quantiles of ff and tt. It amounts to a principled way of either extending the boundaries from [0,1][0,1] to [−u,u+1][-u, u +1] or shrinking them to [u/(2u+1),(u+1)/(2u+1)][u/(2u+1), (u+1)/(2u+1)].Thus, we can choose between an extended- versus a shrunken-support interpretation of this censored-distribution model.

That said, it is not always clear when we should prefer one over the other. The extended-support interpretation infers from the observed spikes at 0 and at 1 that we have underestimated the breadth of the construct. One shrunken-support interpretation might be that people whose responses are near the boundaries have “rounded off” their responses to sit on the boundaries (e.g., someone whose subjective probability assignment is 0.95 has rounded it off to 1). Another interpretation is to infer that the scale is too sensitive to midrange values at the sacrifice of sensitivity to extreme values and needs to be compressed to make room for its genuine tails near 0 and 1.
